newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Zeneca profit to hit 1 bln stg.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Zeneca profit to hit 1 bln stg.

text.p: British bioscience company Zeneca group Plc is expected to break through the 1 billion stg profit barrier for the first time when it announces its 1996 results on March 11, analysts said on Friday.
Pre-tax profit forecasts for the group range narrowly between 992 million and 1.010 billion stg, with a majority of analysts clustered just above the 1.0 billion stg level.
The figure will be a huge advance on the 619 million pounds reported for 1995, which was depressed by 259 million pounds of charges for restructuring, goodwill write-offs and losses on disposals.

Full-year results will be affected by a 35 million reorganisation charge on specialty disposals, signalled at the half-year stage, while reorganisation of its seeds joint venture should cost Zeneca around 20 million stg, analysts said.
The dividend is expected to rise to between 34.5 pence and 37.0 pence from 31.0 pence in 1995.
Analysts said they expected few surprises from the results, which were clearly flagged in a detailed fourth-quarter trading statement on January 28.

Strong pharmaceutical sales are expected to be the main driver, with sales volumes ahead by around 14 percent year-on-year. Zeneca said in January that sales of its biggest-selling drug, cardiovascular treatment Zestril, were ahead by around 12 percent, while prostate cancer drug Zoladex also enjoyed strong growth in 1996.
Attention will also focus on the performance of newer products, particularly another prostate cancer drug Casodex and breast cancer treatment Arimidex.
Sales figures for Accolate, the first of a new generation of asthma drugs taken as tablets, will also be closely watched, not least by competitors waiting to launch similar products.
The group's agrochemcial business is also expected to show strong growth in sales and profits. The company said in January that sales were ahead by around 14 percent in 1996.
One analyst said he would be watching for further clarification of the impact of a stronger pound on the group's 1997 results.

Another analyst said she would be watching for details on the group's research and development pipeline in both pharmaceuticals and agro-chemicals, and expressed concern that the company appeared to have no follow-up products to its strong cardiovascular portfolio.
